rounds.text: Sportking India Ltd is currently undergoing a significant structural transformation that is not fully reflected in its current valuation. The company is aggressively expanding its production capacity with a 150,000-spindle greenfield project in Odisha, which is expected to reach 90% utilization by March [E77, E90]. This expansion is strategically designed to be highly accretive, with management projecting EBITDA margins 300 to 400 basis points higher than existing plants due to embedded incentives [E80]. Furthermore, the company has successfully operationalized solar power projects that are expected to reduce annual power costs by 12% to 15% [E76, E79]. These operational improvements are supported by robust financial health, evidenced by a strong cash conversion ratio of 2.43x and operating cash flow of Rs 292 Cr in March 2026 [E33, E34]. Conceded: the company faces headwinds from global cotton price turbulence and macroeconomic uncertainty [E86, E87], and the current P/B ratio of 2.5x sits above the sector benchmark of 1.25x [E7]. Despite these challenges, the company’s ability to grow its top line to a projected Rs 4,000 Cr next year suggests that the market may be underestimating the impact of these capital-intensive growth initiatives [E70].

The current valuation of Sportking India Ltd appears disconnected from its underlying financial performance, as evidenced by a discounted cash flow analysis that places the intrinsic value at Rs 188 per share, below the current market price of Rs 204 [E44]. This results in a negative margin of safety of -8.8%, suggesting that the market is pricing in future growth that may not materialize [E45]. Furthermore, the company’s recent price appreciation has significantly outpaced its profit growth, with expectations running 72% ahead of actual delivery [E56]. While the company has seen some recent profit recovery, the compounded profit growth over the last three years remains negative at -8%, highlighting a volatile and inconsistent earnings track record [E20]. Conceded: the company has demonstrated strong recent operating cash flow and a positive trend in operating margins [E30, E34]. Investors should also remain cautious of the broader macro uncertainty and inflationary pressures that management has explicitly identified as headwinds to growth [E87, E88].

The bear’s reliance on a static DCF [E44] ignores the company’s explicit forward-looking guidance, which projects revenue growth from 3,000 crores this year to over 4,000 crores next year [E70]. While the bear cites a negative margin of safety [E45], this fails to account for the massive 300 to 400 basis point margin accretion expected from the new Odisha plant [E80] and the immediate cost savings from the newly operational solar projects [E76, E78]. Conceded: the three-year compounded profit growth is -8% [E20]. However, this backward-looking metric is eclipsed by the most recent data, which shows a 37% jump in TTM profit growth [E21] and a significant 7 percentage point increase in quarterly operating margins [E30]. The claim that expectations are running ahead of delivery [E56] is contradicted by the company’s 120% operating cash flow to operating profit ratio [E36], proving that current earnings are backed by tangible cash [E33]. Finally, while the bear highlights macro uncertainty [E87, E88], management has confirmed that demand remains healthy across all markets [E73] and that the company is already operating at near-optimum capacity [E83], positioning it to capture growth immediately upon the commissioning of its greenfield expansion [E77].

Conceded: TTM profit growth reached 37% [E21] and the operating cash flow to operating profit ratio hit 120% [E36]. However, the bull's dismissal of the DCF model's negative -8.8% margin of safety [E44, E45] as a static metric overlooks the historical reality that three-year compounded profit growth contracted by -8% [E20] and five-year profit growth stalled at just 4% [E19]. While the bull leans heavily on management's forward-looking revenue guidance of over 4,000 crores next year [E70], three-year compounded sales growth has slowed to a meagre 4% [E16], proving that past multi-year execution has frequently lagged ambitious projections. Furthermore, the reliance on future margin accretion from the Odisha plant [E80] ignores the company's acknowledged vulnerability to global cotton price turbulence [E86] and the macro headwinds of inflation forecasts and ongoing wars that actively threaten earnings stability [E87, E88]. Finally, the claim that demand remains healthy across all markets [E73] fails to offset the documented volatility in quarterly operating margins, which are explicitly categorized as inconsistent over the last three quarters [E32].

Conceded: the discounted cash flow model yields an intrinsic value of Rs 188 against the market price of Rs 204, resulting in a -8.8% margin of safety [E44, E45]. However, the bear's reliance on historical three-year profit contraction of -8% [E20] and stalled five-year growth [E19] ignores the explosive recent inflection shown by a 37% TTM profit surge [E21] and a top-tier relative-strength rating of 100 [E50]. Similarly, pointing to a 4% three-year sales growth rate [E16] dismisses the concrete reality that the company is already operating near optimal capacity at 95% to 96% [E83], rendering past volume constraints irrelevant to the massive upcoming expansion. While the bear highlights global cotton turbulence [E86] and macro headwinds [E87, E88], management has already insulated margins by successfully launching commercial operations at its solar power project [E76], which generates annual savings of Rs 14 crores to Rs 15 crores [E78]. Finally, the characterization of quarterly margins as inconsistent [E32] overlooks the powerful trend of structural margin expansion, evidenced by operating margins rising to 19% in June 2026 from 12% in the prior-year quarter [E30] alongside stellar cash conversion of 2.43x [E33].

Conceded: operating margins reached 19% in June 2026 compared to 12% a year prior [E30], and the solar project has commenced commercial operations [E76]. However, the bull's dismissal of historical metrics ignores that three-year compounded profit growth sits at -8% [E20], three-year sales growth is a sluggish 4% [E16], and five-year profit growth is only 4% [E19]. Furthermore, while the bull highlights operating near full capacity [E83] to justify future expansion, the market price of Rs 204 already exceeds the DCF intrinsic value of Rs 188 [E44], creating a negative margin of safety of -8.8% [E45]. The reverse DCF confirms that today's price already prices in 5.2% earnings growth, which outpaces the base case assumption of 4.0% [E46]. Finally, celebrating recent price momentum and a relative strength of 100 [E50] ignores the reality that long-term price and profit growth are merely balanced as price-led expectations run ahead of delivery [E55, E56], alongside a severe historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -54.4% [E52].

evidence.quote: We don't -- they'll be -- they shall be -- we are looking at quarter-on-quarter expanding by at least 15%, 20%.

evidence.fact: Demand from all markets continued to remain healthy, and management is encouraged by the outlook going into the second quarter.
evidence.quote: Demand from all the markets continued to remain healthy, and we are also encouraged by the outlook going into the second quarter.

evidence.quote: On the domestic front, we expect demand to remain supportive in the coming quarters, aided by the festive season and improving consumption trends.

evidence.quote: So most of the incremental demand, which has come into India for yarn export is from China.

evidence.fact: The solar power projects have successfully commenced commercial operations.
evidence.quote: On the strategic front, I'm pleased to share that our solar power projects have successfully commenced commercial operations.

evidence.fact: The 150,000-spindle greenfield expansion project in Odisha is progressing as planned with construction activities underway.
evidence.quote: Our 150,000-spindle greenfield expansion project in Odisha is also progressing as planned. We are very excited with that. Construction activities is underway and the first phase of production is expected to commence during the third quarter of the current financial year and we intend to finish our whole project within this financial year.

evidence.fact: The 40-megawatt solar power supply will commence by the end of May and is expected to save INR14 crores to INR15 crores annually.
evidence.quote: The 40-megawatt solar power supply will commence by the end of May and is expected to save around INR14 crores to INR15 crores next year, this -- annually.

evidence.fact: The solar power project is expected to reduce annual power cost by approximately 12% to 15%.
evidence.quote: The project is expected to reduce our annual power cost by approximately 12% to 15%, while simultaneously increasing the share of renewable energy in our overall power consumption.

evidence.fact: The Odisha plant has embedded incentives and is expected to yield EBITDA margins 300 to 400 basis points or more higher than old plants.
evidence.quote: So about EBITDA accretion, this plant has many incentives which are embedded. So we expect the margins coming out of that plant to be at least 300 to 400 basis points or even more than what we do in our old plants.

evidence.fact: The annual cost savings from the solar park are expected to be around 15 crores.
evidence.quote: It should be around INR15 crores with this solar park, yes.

evidence.fact: The company maintains an order book ranging from 70 to 90 days.
evidence.quote: We have an order book ranging from 70 to 90 days in any year, whether it is this year or even the last year or whichever year because this is our policy we work to manage our risk of having higher inventory.

evidence.fact: The company is already operating at optimum capacity of 95%, 96%.
evidence.quote: Volume-wise, we don't see any increase in volume because we are already working at full capacity, whatever is optimum capacity, 95%, 96%.

evidence.fact: The greenfield spindle capacity of 150,000 will take 6 months from commissioning to achieve 97%, 98% utilization.
evidence.quote: I think the day we start commissioning, it should take 6 months from there where we can fully - - when we can expect 97%, 98% utilization.

evidence.fact: Advances for machinery have been released for the greenfield expansion project.
evidence.quote: The land acquisition has been completed, advances of machinery have been released and the construction activities are progressing as scheduled.

evidence.quote: While global cotton prices have shown some turbulence in recent months, we remain focused on prudent procurement and efficient inventory management.
